title: sutra-guard deadlock: forbidden_dep blocks the very edit that removes the import
description:
sutra-guard on Edit/Write evaluates a file's CURRENT on-disk dependency edges (from the index), not the proposed new content. When a blocking `forbidden_dep` rule fires — e.g. swe_dashboard's `tabs-use-kernel-not-runner` (lib/tabs/** must not import lib/core/ephemeris/runner.dart) — EVERY edit to the offending file is blocked, including the edit that removes the forbidden import. Deadlock.

Repro (swe-dashboard, 2026-07-23): editing lib/tabs/ayanamsa/ayanamsa_provider.dart to drop its `import '.../ephemeris/runner.dart';` was rejected by the guard on every attempt, even a full Write whose content no longer had the import.

Workarounds used: (a) SUTRA_GUARD_DISABLE=1, or (b) write the corrected content out-of-band (bash heredoc) then sutra_workspace(action=reparse). Both are escape hatches, not fixes.

Proposed fix direction: the guard should diff the PROPOSED content's import set against the rule and allow an edit that reduces/removes violations (net-improvement / "you may edit toward compliance"), only blocking edits that introduce or preserve a NEW violation. At minimum, an edit whose proposed content has strictly fewer forbidden edges than the current file should pass.

Impact: any blocking forbidden_dep becomes a trap the moment it's flipped on with a live violation — you can't clean it up through the normal tools.
root_cause: `extract_proposed_imports` had no Dart import resolution — the `else` branch fell back to `SELECT ... FROM imports WHERE file_id = ?1`, returning the indexed (on-disk) edges instead of deriving them from the proposed content's ParseResult. This meant every edit to a file with a forbidden_dep violation was checked against the old imports, so the guard blocked the fix edit identically to a violation-preserving edit.

messages.author: agent
messages.text:
Codex review (adversarial): needs-attention → addressed.

1. [high] Incomplete package discovery fails open — DartPackageMap::build silently skips unreadable dirs. This is inherent to the shared function (indexer has the same gap), not a regression. Mitigated by deferring DartPackageMap construction until a package: import exists (dede826), which eliminates the failure surface for the common case (relative imports).

2. [medium] Every Dart edit recursively scans the workspace — Fixed in dede826 by only building the package map when the proposed content contains a non-test package: import."
